sources.entry: Jet Browser - Portable WPE WebKit runtime for agents with isolated Docker sessions, native input, DOM/text reads, fresh screenshots, and ordered JSONL, MCP, and JavaScript SDK interfaces. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: Jet Browser is a standalone WPE WebKit browser runtime, with a Rust WebDriver bridge, that runs one isolated browser session per Docker container and is driven by ordered JSONL commands.
summary.what_it_does: It packages WPE WebKit 2.54 on a headless Wayland compositor (Weston) with a Rust WebDriver bridge as a standalone runtime. Each container runs one browser session and reads one JSON command per input line, returning one JSON response per output line. Supported operations include create, navigate, document state, semantic DOM snapshot, JavaScript evaluation, and PNG screenshots. Native input covers pointer, keyboard, text, touch, wheel, drag, navigation, and tabs. It also provides cookie and web-storage import/export with explicit profile paths, bounded downloads, and versioned JSON Schema tool declarations. The README states that no account, API key, model, or hosted control plane is required, and that the core is not an LLM or agent framework.
use_cases: Running browser actions for an AI agent without bundling a model
Deterministic browser tests driven from CI or a test runner
Isolated disposable browser sessions per untrusted task
Verifying a page with native input, DOM state, and a screenshot
Non-Chromium browser testing with WPE WebKit
Embedding browser control in a Python or Node supervisor process
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <URL from README> | sh  (Docker only; runs network-disabled smoke verification)
npm ci && npm test && cargo test --all-targets  (source development)
notable: One disposable, resource-bounded browser session per container with networking disabled by default in examples
Non-Chromium engine (WPE WebKit) as an alternative to Chromium/CDP-based browser stacks
Ordered line-delimited JSON protocol over stdin/stdout with no required daemon, database, or cloud API
Published MCP server, Codex/Claude Code plugin, Hermes plugin, and GitHub Marketplace Action for verification
Reproducible runtime benchmark and stability test scenario with machine-readable reports
caveats: Does not attach to a daily Chrome profile, does not support Chromium-only extension, policy, or CDP contracts, and does not include a model or agent
Docker socket mounts grant host-level control; the MCP verifier should only be used with a trusted local client
Self-hosted GitHub runners must already permit unprivileged user namespaces for the Action; the README says the Action does not change runner settings
Source builds and the SDK paths require Node.js 24+ and Docker; on AppArmor hosts the outer container AppArmor profile is disabled
keywords: let my agent control a browser
take a screenshot of a page from code
